blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Sen. Mark Villar welcomed on Wednesday the recent passage on third reading at the Senate of the proposed Child Tourist Safety Act (Senate Bill No. 1926), which seeks to strengthen safety standards, emergency preparedness, and access to medical assistance in tourism destinations. The bill is also known as “Sandy’s Act,” after six-year-old Sandy O. Garovillas, who suffered a fatal allergic reaction after being stung by a jellyfish in Port Barton, San Vicente, Palawan, in 2023. “Sandy is only one of many nameless tourists who met their end while vacationing in spots lacking immediate medical aid and emergency response,” […]...
